title: Root-Based Lexicography & Dictionary Mechanics
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 33; Ryding Appendix I)
objectives: Strip augmented letters (ḥurūf al-ziyādah: س أ ل ت م و ن ي ه ا) to isolate the triliteral root.
Restore weak, doubled, and assimilated radicals before looking up words in Hans Wehr or Lane's Lexicon.
Navigate dictionary entries organized by Form I → Forms II–X → derived nouns.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 22: Under which letter do you look up اِتَّقَى in a root-based Arabic dictionary?

sections.heading: How Classical Arabic Dictionaries Are Organized
sections.body: Unlike English dictionaries (which alphabetize by spelling), classical and scholarly Arabic dictionaries—such as Hans Wehr, Lane's Arabic-English Lexicon, and Lisān al-ʿArab—arrange all words under their 3-consonant (or 4-consonant) root. To look up any word, you must first strip prefixes, infixes, and suffixes.

sections.label: 4-Step Root Extraction Method
sections.summary: 1) Strip inflectional prefixes/suffixes (أَلْ, بـ, تـ, ـون, ـات, ـة). 2) Strip derivational augments (حُرُوفُ الزِّيَادَةِ, mnemonic: سَأَلْتُمُونِيهَا). 3) If fewer than 3 consonants remain, restore an elided weak radical (و/ي), uncontract a shaddah, or check Form VIII تّ → و. 4) Look up the root in alphabetical order.

sections.irab: اِسْتِقَامَةٌ: مَصْدَرُ العَاشِرِ مِنْ جَذْرِ (ق-و-م) أَصْلُهُ اِسْتِقْوَامٌ
sections.notes: Because ق-و-م is hollow, Form X maṣdar (اِسْتِفْعَالٌ) drops the wāw into long ā and adds ة: اِسْتِقَامَةٌ.

sections.heading: Try the Root & Pattern Explorer
sections.body: Practice stripping augmented letters interactively in Grammar Tools → Root & Pattern Explorer.
